clue.text: One down in feeble defensive construction

indicators.note: the words before it are placed inside the word for feeble

parts.note: feeble means pale, as in a pale imitation
the Roman numeral for one is I
down means sad, low in spirits

explanation.surface: A sorry defence that has one man feeling low inside a weak fortification.
explanation.walkthrough: 'down' is an adjective for low spirits here, not a direction; 'in' does the containing.
explanation.definitionFit: A palisade is a fence of pointed stakes built to keep attackers out.

clue.text: It's turned up in nasty cheap copy

indicators.note: in places the turned word inside the scrambled letters
nasty suggests the letters are mangled
in a down clue, turned up means read from bottom to top

explanation.surface: A shoddy, tacky imitation has turned up.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'turned up' reads ITS bottom to top; 'nasty' makes PACHE, split around it by 'in'.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastiche is a work imitating the style of another, a kind of copy.

clue.text: Failure surprisingly exposing requirements of angler

indicators.note: exposing reveals letters sitting within the words

explanation.surface: A surprising flop shows what a fisherman really needs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exposing' reveals 'faiLURE Surprisingly'; 'surprisingly' is not an anagram signal here.
explanation.definitionFit: Lures are artificial baits an angler needs to attract fish.

clue.text: Bowlers losing power? They've done something wrong!

indicators.note: losing means the letter for power drops out

parts.note: spinners are slow bowlers in cricket, who make the ball turn
P is the physics abbreviation for power

explanation.surface: Cricket bowlers who have lost their potency must have misbehaved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing' removes P from SPINNERS. Spinners are cricket bowlers who make the ball turn.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinners are people who have transgressed, done wrong in a moral sense.

clue.text: Heartless benefactor's opportunity

indicators.note: heartless removes the central letter of the word

parts.note: a donor is a benefactor

explanation.surface: A cold-hearted patron gets his chance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartless' removes N, the middle of DONOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A door is figuratively an opening or opportunity, as in a door to success.

clue.text: Dilemmas resulting from robberies, say with son in for millions

indicators.note: one letter goes in where the other was, standing in for it

parts.note: robberies are examples of crimes
M is the abbreviation for million(s)
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: Awkward situations arise when thefts happen, with someone's son involved instead of millions of pounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in for' swaps the M of CRIMES for S.
explanation.definitionFit: Crises are critical turning points, moments of dire difficulty like a dilemma.

clue.text: Hercules failed, missing first one avoiding others

indicators.note: failed suggests the letters have broken down and fallen into disorder
missing first drops the opening letter of the hero's name

explanation.surface: The mighty hero Hercules flopped, missing out on first place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing first' drops H; 'failed' scrambles ERCULES.
explanation.definitionFit: A recluse lives alone and shuns company, avoiding other people.

clue.text: Dish from poor area mostly in part of Iberia (not north)

indicators.note: in places the shortened slum word inside the country
not north removes the N for north

parts.note: Spain is part of the Iberian peninsula

indicators.note: mostly drops the final letter

parts.note: a ghetto is a poor area of a city

explanation.surface: A meal hails from a deprived district somewhere in Spain or Portugal.
explanation.walkthrough: Iberia is the peninsula holding Spain and Portugal; 'mostly' and 'not north' each trim a letter, and 'in' nests one result in the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Spaghetti is a pasta dish of long thin strands.

clue.text: Films about European geese

indicators.note: the films word goes around the letter

parts.note: a skin is a thin film on a surface

explanation.surface: Movies about European geese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts E inside SKINS. 'Films' means thin layers, not movies.
explanation.definitionFit: A skein is a flock of wild geese in flight.

clue.text: Make last call on way public

indicators.note: on here says the call word sits after the way word in the answer

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way
to ring is to call on the phone
out means public, no longer secret

explanation.surface: Telephoning someone on the street and going public with the news.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' sets the call word after the way word; 'last' is a verb, endure, not 'final'.
explanation.definitionFit: To string out something is to prolong or eke it out so it lasts longer.

clue.text: Rough speed on a road

parts.note: to tear is to speed along
a way is a road

explanation.surface: Bumpy speeding on a road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' just joins the pieces. 'Rough' is a noun, a ruffian.
explanation.definitionFit: A tearaway is a wild, reckless young person, a rough or hooligan.

clue.text: Stop those ultimately involved in legal action

indicators.note: the letter is wrapped up inside the lawsuit word

parts.note: a case is a lawsuit, a legal action

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word those

explanation.surface: Telling certain people mixed up in a lawsuit to desist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' gives E from 'those'; 'involved in' puts it inside CASE.
explanation.definitionFit: To cease is to halt or come to an end, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Measure on the inside of wing arch

parts.note: on the inside means in
a step is a measure, a course of action taken

explanation.surface: Taking measurements inside a car's wing arch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of wing' is surface padding; the definition is 'arch', the instep being the arched part of the foot.
explanation.definitionFit: The instep is the raised, arched middle part of the human foot.

clue.text: Do better than street kid, losing right man in order

parts.note: to cap something is to outdo it

indicators.note: losing tells us a letter drops out of the urchin word

parts.note: an urchin is a scruffy child of the streets

explanation.surface: Outshining a street urchin who has lost the right sort of man to keep things in order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing' removes R from URCHIN, leaving UCHIN. An 'order' here is a religious order.
explanation.definitionFit: A Capuchin is a friar of a Franciscan religious order, so a man in an order.

clue.text: Second design of replica vent for breathing

indicators.note: a design of the letters is a new arrangement of them

explanation.surface: A second blueprint for a copy of a breathing vent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'design of' rearranges REPLICA into PIRACLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A spiracle is a breathing hole in insects or a blowhole in whales.

clue.text: Those who will succeed needing husband and father perhaps to embrace high praise

indicators.note: the outer pieces hug the scrambled letters between them

parts.note: a father is an example of a parent

indicators.note: high, as in intoxicated, signals the letters are muddled up

explanation.surface: Successors need a husband and a dad who will lavish praise on them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'high' (as in drunk) is the anagram signal, making EIRSAP; 'to embrace' has the husband and father pieces hold it between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Heirs apparent are next in line to inherit, who will succeed to a title or estate.

clue.text: Meaning one in Paris could be bother

parts.note: import means meaning or significance
une is French for one

explanation.surface: A word meaning one in French could be a nuisance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' just links wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To importune is to pester someone with repeated requests.

clue.text: Set out to carry freight — delicacy from France

indicators.note: the scrambled letters hold the freight word between them
out tells us the letters are put out of order

parts.note: cargo is freight

explanation.surface: Setting out to transport goods, a French treat on board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set out' looks like one phrase, but 'out' scrambles SET into EST, and 'to carry' has it hold the freight word.
explanation.definitionFit: Escargot is the French name for snails cooked as a delicacy.

clue.text: Head of house seen as impartial and safe, somehow

indicators.note: somehow says the letters come together in some unspecified new order

explanation.surface: The man of the house is regarded as fair and dependable.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram indicator rearranges IMPARTIAL and SAFE together.
explanation.definitionFit: Paterfamilias is Latin for the father of the family, its male head.

clue.text: Content at last, turned round and did some fishing

indicators.note: at last picks the final letter of content

parts.note: rolled means turned over and over

explanation.surface: Finally satisfied, the angler turned about and cast a line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at last' gives T from 'Content'.
explanation.definitionFit: To troll is to fish by trailing a baited line behind a boat.

clue.text: Popular present, for example, that's heavy!

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
the present is an example of a grammatical tense

explanation.surface: A fashionable gift that weighs a ton!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Present' is a grammatical tense, not a gift.
explanation.definitionFit: Heavy in its slang sense means intense or serious, as in a heavy conversation.

clue.text: Drugs needed for teeth

definitions.meaning: the upper teeth, especially a set of upper dentures

explanation.surface: Pills required for one's teeth.
explanation.definitionFit: Uppers are both stimulant pills and the top row of teeth or dentures.

clue.text: Crew leaving show, inevitably

indicators.note: leaving means the crew word departs from the show word

parts.note: a performance is a show
to man is to crew, as with a ship

explanation.surface: The crew walk out of the production, as was bound to happen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' removes MAN from PERFORMANCE. 'Crew' is a verb here, not a group of people.
explanation.definitionFit: Perforce is an old adverb meaning necessarily or by force of circumstance.

clue.text: Answer coming after Laurel's reported lines

indicators.note: the answer letter follows the other piece
reported means we hear the word spoken rather than see it

parts.note: Stan Laurel was the thin half of Laurel and Hardy, so Laurel's is Stan's

explanation.surface: A reply follows what the comedian Laurel is said to have uttered.
explanation.walkthrough: STAN'S said out loud gives STANZ; A comes after it.
explanation.definitionFit: A stanza is a group of lines forming a verse of a poem.

clue.text: Born yesterday — this person in main part of church

indicators.note: in puts the self-reference inside the church part

parts.note: the nave is the main body of a church
this person is the setter, I

explanation.surface: An innocent newcomer stands in the body of the church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this person' means the setter, I.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone 'born yesterday' is gullible and inexperienced, which is naive.

clue.text: A note that's added on the end of late recess

parts.note: PS, postscript, is a note added at the end of a letter

indicators.note: on the end of picks the final letter of late

explanation.surface: A late postscript added to a note about a holiday break.
explanation.walkthrough: PS is a postscript; 'on the end of' gives E from 'late'.
explanation.definitionFit: An apse is a semicircular recess, usually at the east end of a church.

clue.text: Rare quality defining peer

indicators.note: the answer is contained within the words, which mark out its limits

explanation.surface: An uncommon trait that marks out a member of the nobility.
explanation.walkthrough: 'defining' signals EQUAL inside 'raRE QUALity'. 'Peer' looks like a lord but means an equal.
explanation.definitionFit: A peer is someone of equal standing, as in a jury of one's peers.

clue.text: Laying out previous conclusion about source of pandemic

parts.note: ex means former or previous

indicators.note: source of picks the first letter of pandemic

parts.note: an ending is a conclusion

explanation.surface: Setting out an earlier verdict on where the pandemic began.
explanation.walkthrough: 'source of' gives P from 'pandemic'; 'about' just joins it, the conclusion being about that source.
explanation.definitionFit: Laying out money means spending it, so expending is the synonym.

clue.text: Fragments of pitcher finally found in outhouses

indicators.note: found in puts the letter inside the outhouses word

parts.note: sheds are outhouses

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of pitcher

explanation.surface: Shards of a broken jug turn up in garden buildings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' gives R from 'pitcher'; 'found in' puts it inside SHEDS.
explanation.definitionFit: Sherds is a variant of shards, broken pieces of pottery found by archaeologists.

clue.text: Respectful of lease always being accepted

indicators.note: the word for always is taken in by the lease word

parts.note: to rent is to lease
ever means always

explanation.surface: Courteous about a lease that is renewed in perpetuity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being accepted' signals one word taken inside the other; 'of' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Reverent means showing deep respect, as in worship.
